Package frc.lib.NinjasLib.controllers

Class SimulatedController

java.lang.Object
frc.lib.NinjasLib.controllers.Controller
frc.lib.NinjasLib.controllers.SimulatedController
public class SimulatedController extends Controller
A Controller implementation for simulation: instead of talking to real motor hardware, it drives a WPILib LinearSystemSim (an ElevatorSim, SingleJointedArmSim, DCMotorSim, FlywheelSim, or a custom subclass, supplied via ControllerConstants.simSystem) and runs its own PIDController/ ProfiledPIDController/TrapezoidProfile in software to emulate the closed-loop behavior real motor controller firmware would otherwise provide. Created automatically by Controller.createController(ControllerType, ControllerConstants) when not running on a real robot.

    SimulatedController(ControllerConstants constants)
    Builds the simulated mechanism from ControllerConstants.simSystem (detecting which LinearSystemSim subclass it is so position/velocity/current reads can be dispatched correctly), and sets up the software trapezoid profile and PID controllers used to emulate closed-loop control per ControllerConstants.real's controlConstants.

    periodic()
    Advances the simulation by one 20ms loop: since a simulated mechanism has no real motor controller firmware running its closed loop, this method performs that role in software - computing an input voltage from the profiled PID controller, plain PID controller, or trapezoid profile depending on the configured ControlType, applying it, clamping the mechanism to its configured soft limits, updating the acceleration estimate, and stepping the underlying LinearSystemSim.

    • periodic

      public void periodic()
      Advances the simulation by one 20ms loop: since a simulated mechanism has no real motor controller firmware running its closed loop, this method performs that role in software - computing an input voltage from the profiled PID controller, plain PID controller, or trapezoid profile depending on the configured ControlType, applying it, clamping the mechanism to its configured soft limits, updating the acceleration estimate, and stepping the underlying LinearSystemSim. Call this from the owning subsystem's simulationPeriodic().
